evidence:
Built a requirement-to-criterion map from instruction.md and hireops_rules.md sections 1-9 against 43 Functional, 5 Polish, 5 Visual criteria and 2 gates. Coverage is broad and mostly strong: job validation (hro_job_open); intake, email rules, account link (hro_add_candidate, hro_add_email_rules, hro_candidate_linked); one-stage, skip, bottom arrival, reorder (hro_move_one_stage, hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder); reject, hired, reopen incl. undo restoring the reason (hro_reject_reason, hro_reject_hired, hro_reopen); Interview places incl. bulk and undo (hro_interview_full, hro_interview_reorder_free, hro_bulk_places, hro_undo_full); refused put-back with focus (hro_refused_put_back); every HM/observer/candidate/anonymous role rule and 401/403/404/409 (hro_mgr_*, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous, hro_refusal_status); bulk all-or-none and board order (hro_bulk_move, hro_bulk_all_or_none); undo is per person (protocol L: Mei's later move does not become Rafael's undo target), a note is not a change, a later move invalidates, undo once (hro_undo_restores, hro_undo_conflict, hro_undo_once); Activity incl. refusals and observer (hro_activity, hro_activity_refusals); notes (hro_notes); live updates and preservation (hro_live_board, hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread); messages, compose, failed send (hro_msg_exchange, hro_msg_compose, hro_pol_failed_send); paging and anchoring (hro_thread_latest, hro_thread_earlier, hro_pol_earlier_place); unread incl. sending-counts-as-read via Mei's expected count and Lena's seeded marker (hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up); seen incl. observer exclusion and HM (hro_seen); drafts incl. session end and another user on the same browser, plus note drafts (hro_drafts, hro_pol_session_resume); candidate view and privacy (hro_candidate_view, hro_candidate_private); restart and seed-once (hro_restart); desktop visual quality (5 Likert rows). The whole-flow bundling false positive was respected; none of the items below is a bundling complaint.

GAPS (asked for, not graded):

G1 (P2) User-visible stale-move feedback. instruction.md:3 'If a move is refused, put the card back where it really is and tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who.' and hireops_rules.md:79-81 'Tell them the card was changed and by whom, and show the card where it really is.' Protocol C (tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:41) only replays the captured request via fetch, so no stale refusal ever happens in the UI, and hro_stale_refused (functional/judge.toml:211) accepts the name 'by name in the response or on screen'. hro_refused_put_back (judge.toml:139) covers UI put-back, reason and focus only for the full-Interview refusal. Whether the user is ever told WHO changed the card, or sees the stale card put back on the mover's page, is therefore ungraded; a JSON field suffices.

G2 (P3) Form retention after an email refusal covers only name and email. hireops_rules.md:35-36 'tell us at that field and keep whatever was typed, so nobody retypes the form'; hro_add_email_rules (judge.toml:49) checks 'the typed name and email stay in the form' and protocol S (prompt.md:35) says 'typed name kept'. The source field is never checked after a refusal.

G3 (P3) Undo of a rejection, or of a re-order, is never exercised. hireops_rules.md:98-99 'Undo puts every card of that move back in the stage and the place it came from, and gives back a rejection reason the move removed'. Undo of a reopening is tested (hro_reopen) and stage moves are tested, but undoing a reject (card back to its prior stage and place) and undoing a re-order are not. Somewhat ambiguous whether 'move' includes reject and re-order: Activity (rules:113) lists them separately, while rules:51-52 calls rejection a move.

Representative-only, recorded as notes rather than gaps: undo blocked by an intervening 'reopened' (rules:100) has no separate leg (moved, re-ordered and rejected do); bulk 'Each card still has to follow every rule above' (rules:93-94) is exercised for skip and places only, not HM role or stale version inside a set; draft and cursor preservation 'whether I am reading or halfway through a reply' (instruction.md:7) is checked only at the newest message (hro_pol_live_thread), the scrolled-up case checks place only (hro_unread_scrolled_up); 'signing in doesn't open one for them' (rules:185-186) is only indirectly covered by Lena's unread=1 reading in Z; 'start with no shipped database' and 'GET /api/health ... never touches the database' (instruction.md:15,17) are runtime-contract items not graded by any criterion (test.sh only probes /api/health for readiness and copies /app wholesale, so a shipped app.db would go unnoticed) and belong to shared runtime policy / deterministic rows rather than judge criteria; Node/Express/SQLite comes from template integration.md, is not browser-provable and is correctly not judge-graded.

Colderwater lessons checked for this row: lesson 1 and 18 (every brief demand needs a criterion; fixes can open gaps) -> G1-G3; lesson 15 (restart re-reads several records) -> hro_restart reads jobs, order, notes, messages, unread and activity, no gap; lesson 16 (double grading) -> ownership is assigned explicitly, not a coverage issue.

No runtime run is needed for this source-coverage row; scripted golden evidence in raw-evidence-index.json is not used as proof of coverage, and no Oracle/model/portal score is implied.
counterexample: An app whose server answers the stale move with 409 {error:'Card was changed', changedBy:'Mei Lin'} but whose UI on any 409 shows only 'Move failed' and leaves the optimistic card position until the next poll, whose add-candidate form resets the Source field after an email refusal, and which cannot undo a rejection, passes hro_stale_refused (name present in the response), hro_add_email_rules (name and email kept) and every undo row, while violating instruction.md:3 'tell me who', hireops_rules.md:36 'keep whatever was typed' and hireops_rules.md:98-99 for rejections.
suggested_fix: G1: require the changer's name and the card's real place to be shown on screen for a stale refusal (drop 'in the response or' from hro_stale_refused and add a feasible UI leg, e.g. the stale move made from a second Rafael page whose board has not yet refreshed), or soften the public wording if only server-side identification is intended; G2: add 'and source' to hro_add_email_rules and protocol S; G3: add an undo-of-rejection leg (card returns to its prior stage and place) to an existing undo row, or state in the rules which actions are undoable. Re-review rows 27, 28, 30, 32 and workload after any change.
